heard: Sunlight bending through Venus's atmosphere creates a glowing halo. We all know the Moon shifts from full disk to thin crescent. Galileo Galilei proved in 1610 that Venus undergoes identical phases. At full phase, Venus spans under 10 arcseconds from Earth. Near Earth, its crescent swells to over 60 arcseconds. Galileo even hid his discovery in a scrambled Latin anagram. Astronomers caught another jaw-dropping effect during the 1761 transit. Thick atmosphere refracts sunlight straight around the planet's edge. Before entering the sun's disc, light encircles the entire world.
